Breaches involving a third party doubled in a year, to 30%.

Every supplier with access to your systems is part of your attack surface.

What to do this week:
1. Remove supplier access nobody uses.
2. Give suppliers only the access they need.

Source: Verizon Data Breach Investigations Report 2025

It takes 241 days to identify and contain a typical breach.

That's roughly eight months. Testing finds the gap before someone else spends that time inside it.

What to do this week:
1. Switch on logging and actually review it.
2. Test whether an intruder would be noticed.

Source: IBM Cost of a Data Breach Report 2025

Exploited vulnerabilities were the way in for 20% of breaches.

That's up 34% in a year. Unpatched software is an open door with a sign on it.

What to do this week:
1. Patch internet-facing software first.
2. Switch off systems you no longer use.

Source: Verizon Data Breach Investigations Report 2025

Cyber Essentials requires critical and high-risk updates within 14 days.

Fourteen days from the vendor's release. A monthly patch cycle can miss it.

What to do this week:
1. Turn on automatic updates wherever you can.
2. Keep a list of what you run so nothing is missed.

Source: NCSC, Cyber Essentials requirements for IT infrastructure

What to do this week:
1. Read the five Cyber Essentials controls.
2. Check your business against each one.

Source: Cyber Security Breaches Survey 2025/26, GOV.UK

Stolen or abused credentials were the way in for 22% of breaches.

Reused passwords still work far too often. Multi-factor authentication makes a stolen password far less useful.

What to do this week:
1. Turn on MFA everywhere it's offered.
2. Use a password manager so nothing is reused.

Source: Verizon Data Breach Investigations Report 2025

What to do this week:
1. Book your next pen test before the year is up.
2. Retest after any major change.

Source: PCI DSS v4.0.1, Requirement 11.4

UK GDPR fines can reach £17.5 million or 4% of global turnover, whichever is higher.

That's the ceiling. Better never to find out what yours would be.

What to do this week:
1. Know what personal data you hold, and why.
2. Only keep what you actually need.

Source: ICO, Data protection fining guidance

What to do this week:
1. Check the five basic controls are in place.
2. Have someone test the locks for you.

Source: NCSC, Cyber Essentials overview
